cells.title: Add bee hook agy-belt that translates agy hook payloads onto the existing bee checks
cells.action: Implement agy-runtime D3, D4 and the belt half of D5. Add hooks/agy_belt.rs and register agy-belt in HOOK_NAMES and the dispatch match in hooks/mod.rs. The module has pure functions plus a thin run(): (1) parse the agy payload (camelCase: hookEventName, conversationId, cwd, workspacePaths, lastUserInput, invocationNum, toolCall {id,name,args}, error, continuationActive); (2) map_tool(name, args) -> a typed enum MappedTool { Check { tool_name, tool_input }, NoWrite, Subagent, Unknown } per D4: run_command {CommandLine} -> Bash {command}; write_file {Path, Content} -> Write {file_path, content}; edit_file {Path, Target, Replacement} -> Edit {file_path, old_string, new_string}; read_file {Path} -> Read {file_path}; invoke_subagent -> Subagent; a named const list of no-write tools (search_web, send_message, call_mcp_tool, read_url_content, list_dir, view_file, list_directory, the plan tool name seen in discovery, every name starting with browser_ or capture_browser or read_browser) -> NoWrite; any other tool carrying Path, AbsolutePath, TargetFile or File -> Check as Write {file_path, content: ""}; else Unknown; (3) build the Claude-shaped payload: hook_event_name, session_id = conversationId, cwd, bee_runtime agy, transcript_path, plus prompt (UserPromptSubmit), tool_name/tool_input (PreToolUse/PostToolUse), stop_hook_active (Stop); (4) run the existing hooks as child processes of std::env::current_exe() with args [hook, <name>] and the translated stdin, capturing stdout and exit status. Which hooks per event: read the Claude projection rows in devtools/hook_manifests.rs CATALOG for that event and tool (the same scripts the Claude plugin wires, mapped to their bee hook names as the existing Claude command builder does) so the belt never hand-lists checks that drift; (5) map answers back: SessionStart and PreInvocation (only invocationNum 0, else print {} and run nothing; PreInvocation maps to UserPromptSubmit with prompt = lastUserInput) -> collect the plain text or systemMessage text of each hook into {"injectSteps":[{"systemMessage":{"systemMessage":text}}]} or {} when empty; PreToolUse -> the first deny (hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision deny, decision block, or exit code 2 with stderr) gives {"decision":"deny","reason":r}; an updatedInput repair gives {"decision":"ask","overwrite":{...}} mapped back to agy keys (command -> CommandLine, file_path -> Path, content -> Content, old_string -> Target, new_string -> Replacement); otherwise {"decision":"ask"}; Subagent -> deny with reason naming bee dispatch prepare --runtime agy --kind cell|gather|reviewer|advisor --json; NoWrite -> ask; Unknown -> ask and append a coverage-gap row with adapter::log_coverage_gap; a crash, a spawn error or an unreadable payload on PreToolUse -> deny (fail closed); PostToolUse -> run the checks, print {}; Stop -> session-close with stop_hook_active = continuationActive; a block (decision block) -> {"decision":"continue","reason":r}, else {}; any failure on a non-PreToolUse event prints the neutral answer and exits 0. Always exit 0 and always print exactly one JSON object. Unit-test every pure function: the tool map for each named tool, the unknown-with-path case, the answer mapping for deny, repair, pass, Stop block, and invocationNum > 0. No code comments.
cells.verify: PATH="${CARGO_HOME:-$HOME/.cargo}/bin:$PATH" cargo test --release --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml -p bee --bin bee agy_belt

must_haves.why: agy sends its own JSON shape, so the existing checks need a translator to guard an agy session.
truths: a PreToolUse run_command that the write guard refuses prints decision deny with the guard's reason
a PreToolUse the checks pass prints decision ask
invoke_subagent is denied with a reason naming bee dispatch prepare --runtime agy --kind cell
a Stop the session-close hook blocks prints decision continue
every run prints exactly one JSON object and exits 0
prohibitions: No hand list of checks that duplicates the catalog

cells.title: Ship the agy belt file and wire it through onboarding and doctor
cells.action: Implement agy-runtime D2 and D7. (1) Add onboard/agy_belt.rs with a pure render_bee_key() -> serde_json::Value for the bee hook name: SessionStart, PreInvocation and Stop as flat handler lists; PreToolUse and PostToolUse as one group with matcher "" and hooks; each handler {"type":"command","command":C,"timeout":30} where C is one POSIX sh line that execs ../.bee/bin/bee hook agy-belt when that file is executable (the hook runs in the .agents folder), else the .bee/bin/bee under the git common dir's parent (the same fallback the Claude wiring uses), else prints the neutral answer for the event ({"decision":"ask"} on PreToolUse, {} elsewhere) so a missing binary never blocks every tool. Add merge_into(existing: Option<&str>) -> Result<String, MergeError>: no file -> {"bee": render}; an object -> replace only key bee, keep every other key's value; a non-object or unparseable file -> MergeError naming the file; output pretty JSON with a trailing newline, stable so a second merge is byte-identical. (2) Wire it into onboarding apply beside copy_pi_extension: plan an agy_belt step when .agents/hooks.json is missing or its bee key differs; back up a pre-existing file to .agents/hooks.json.bee-backup before the first rewrite; refuse with the typed error and write nothing on a malformed file; a settled project plans nothing. Skip it when the target repo is bee's own checkout only if the checked-in file already equals the render. (3) Check in .agents/hooks.json at the repo root, generated by render_bee_key, and add a test that the checked-in file's bee key equals the render. (4) doctor.rs: add an agy wiring row: ok when the bee key equals the render, else names bee onboard --apply as the fix. (5) In devtools/hook_manifests.rs extend the NAMED EXCLUSION text block to agy (no Runtime::Agy; the belt is the projection) without adding comments elsewhere, and add agy to the derived coverage test the same way Pi joins it if that test enumerates belts. Unit-test merge_into: fresh, owner key kept, stale bee key replaced, malformed refused, idempotent. No code comments other than the existing doc block you extend.

cells.title: Document the agy runtime, its belt and team.agy
cells.action: Implement agy-runtime D8 in plain ASD-STE100 English. (1) New concept docs/knowledge/areas/hook-runtime/the-agy-belt.md with the same frontmatter shape as docs/knowledge/areas/hook-runtime/pi-version-pin-and-capability-audit.md (type bee.area, id hook-runtime-the-agy-belt, areas [hook-runtime], decisions citing agy-runtime D1-D8 as the history D-number on one line, sources docs/history/agy-runtime/CONTEXT.md and discovery.md, anchors the files named in CONTEXT.md plus packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/hooks/agy_belt.rs, .agents/hooks.json and packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/onboard/agy_belt.rs, verified_at 2026-11-25). Body: what agy reads (AGENTS.md, .agents/skills, .agents/hooks.json), the bee key and its five events, the translation table per event, the D4 tool map, the ask/deny/continue answers and why an empty answer is never printed (agy denies on {}), invoke_subagent denied and herding-only dispatch, ANTIGRAVITY_CONVERSATION_ID, onboarding merge rules, the owner's one-time workspace trust. Register the concept in docs/knowledge/index.md if the bundle needs it (run bee knowledge index if that is the regen path). (2) In catalog-projections-and-activation.md say there are five runtimes and add one paragraph: agy takes the named exclusion; its belt is .agents/hooks.json plus bee hook agy-belt. (3) In onboarding/repo-local-guardrails.md add one Business Rules bullet for the agy belt merge (D7). (4) docs/config-reference.md: add team.agy beside team.pi. (5) README.md: add agy where the supported runtimes are listed. Write the words without deferral words such as deferred, until or later. No code comments.

must_haves.why: Leaders and owners need to read how agy is wired before they trust it.
truths: a knowledge concept describes the agy belt translation and tool map
the README names agy as a supported runtime
the config reference names team.agy

cells.title: Test the agy belt, the runtime label and the onboarding merge end to end
cells.action: Without reading the implementers' notes, check agyrt-1, agyrt-2 and agyrt-3 against agy-runtime D1-D7 and add integration tests in tests/agy_belt_contracts.rs that drive the built bee binary against a temp git repo onboarded the way the existing integration tests do (see tests/pi_plugin_contracts.rs and tests/opencode_plugin_contracts.rs for the harness). Feed bee hook agy-belt the agy payload shapes recorded in docs/history/agy-runtime/discovery.md and assert: a PreToolUse write_file to a path the write guard refuses (a governed path before the gate, or a secret-shaped file) prints decision deny; an allowed read_file prints decision ask; run_command with a command the CLI-shape or write guard refuses prints deny; invoke_subagent prints deny naming bee dispatch prepare --runtime agy --kind cell; a PreInvocation with invocationNum 0 prints injectSteps and with invocationNum 3 prints {}; SessionStart prints injectSteps with bee text; a Stop prints one JSON object; garbage stdin on PreToolUse prints deny and exit code 0; every output is exactly one JSON object. Run bee onboard --apply on a temp repo with an owner .agents/hooks.json holding a key owner: after apply the owner key is unchanged, the bee key exists, a second apply leaves the bytes equal, and a malformed file is refused and left unchanged. Assert bee dispatch prepare --runtime agy --kind cell with a native slot refuses with the herding remedy. See each new test fail on purpose once (break an assertion) before trusting it. A tester never edits product code: on a defect return BLOCKED with the red output. No code comments.

must_haves.why: A code cell never certifies itself.
truths: a test fails if a refused agy write prints anything but decision deny
a test fails if a passing agy tool call prints an empty object
a test fails if onboarding drops an owner key from .agents/hooks.json
a test fails if invoke_subagent is not denied

cells.title: Correct the agy docs the checker found wrong
cells.action: Fix the three findings in docs/history/agy-runtime/reports/agyrt-6-docs-check.md. (1) docs/config-reference.md team.agy section: the template derives team.agy from team.claude role for role (onboard/templates.rs team.agy block), every slot { kind: herding, agent: agy, description }, and herding.agents carries agy: ["agy"]; replace the example so it shows that shape (a few roles plus a note that every team.claude role is present) and drop the claude-opus, claude-fable and agy-flash agents. (2) the-agy-belt.md advisory failure line: a crash or spawn error of a child hook on SessionStart, PreInvocation, PostToolUse and Stop fails open with the neutral answer; an unreadable payload fails closed on every event with {"decision":"deny","reason":"agy-belt: unreadable hook payload: ..."} because the event is not known before the parse (hooks/agy_belt.rs handle_payload). (3) the-agy-belt.md fallback line: the second lookup is $g/../.bee/bin/bee where $g is the absolute git common dir, so it finds the main checkout's binary from a worktree. Edit only those lines. Run .bee/bin/bee knowledge check. No code comments.

must_haves.why: The agyrt-6 checker found docs that disagree with the shipped code.
truths: the team.agy example matches the onboarding template
the unreadable payload line matches handle_payload

cells.title: Test the agy belt inside a herded worker pane
cells.action: The agyrt-2 judge found that with BEE_HERDING_WORKER=1 set, bee hook agy-belt exited 0 with empty stdout before the belt ran, so an agy herding worker got no PreToolUse answer and no write guard. Without reading the implementer notes, add integration tests in tests/agy_belt_contracts.rs, using the harness that file already has, that run the built bee binary with BEE_HERDING_WORKER=1 in the child env and assert: a PreToolUse list_dir prints exactly one JSON object with decision ask; a PreToolUse write_file to a path the write guard refuses in a herded pane prints decision deny; a PreToolUse invoke_subagent prints decision deny; SessionStart and Stop each print exactly one JSON object and exit 0. See each new test fail on purpose once (break an assertion) before trusting it. A tester never edits product code: on a defect return BLOCKED with the red output. No code comments.

must_haves.why: A code cell never certifies itself, and the herded pane is the path agy workers run on.
truths: a test fails if agy-belt under BEE_HERDING_WORKER prints empty output on PreToolUse
a test fails if a refused agy write under BEE_HERDING_WORKER is not denied
